hops.rationale: The requested goal is tariff and trade-policy risks affecting supply chain costs, within TSLA FY2026 filing scope. Passage 000162828026003952#item1A#passage-000002 states that 2025 U.S. trade policy changes, including heightened import tariffs and retaliatory measures, have impacted supply chain costs and may affect component availability. Passage #item1A#passage-000014 covers U.S. tariff increases, possible renegotiation of trade agreements, retaliatory tariffs, and says historical special tariff actions raised costs for vehicles made in the U.S. and exported. Passage #item7#passage-000000 says evolving trade and fiscal policy poses risks to the global supply chain and cost structure. Passage #item7#passage-000003 says tariff, export-control and trade-policy changes may affect the global supply chain cost structure and availability. Together these state the core requested facts directly. No quantified cost amount was requested, so its absence does not lower the score.

hops.rationale: The TSLA 2026 filing (accession 000162828026003952) fully supports the requested goal, "cost of revenues and gross margin disclosures." Passage 000020 gives the Cost of Revenues and Gross Margin table for 2025, 2024 and 2023: automotive sales, leasing, services and other, energy generation and storage, and total cost of revenues ($77,733M, $80,240M, $79,113M), plus gross profit and gross margin by segment (total automotive 17.8%/18.4%/19.4%; total gross margin 18.0%/17.9%/18.2%). Passages 000021 to 000023 add the consolidated income statement (Total revenues, Total cost of revenues, Gross profit of $17,094M/$17,450M/$17,660M), the energy gross margin (29.8%/26.2%/18.9%), and the year-over-year drivers of cost and margin changes. Tariffs appear only as a cost component in these passages. Tariff risk factors are a separate subquery and were not graded here.
